clue.text: Vicar maybe caught religious artefact changing hands

indicators.note: left and right are the two hands, so the letters standing for left and right trade places

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
a relic is an object venerated as holy

explanation.surface: A vicar is caught passing a holy object from one hand to the other.
explanation.walkthrough: In the artefact's name, R stands for right and L for left, the two hands, so those letters trade places.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicar is one example of a member of the clergy, hence the 'maybe'.

clue.text: Colin's upset and reluctant to be seen in skimpy dress

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and disordered, so the name's letters are rearranged

parts.note: the name taken as written
loth means unwilling or reluctant

explanation.surface: Colin is embarrassed and shy about appearing in revealing clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A loincloth is a minimal garment of cloth wrapped round the hips, about as scanty as clothing gets.

clue.text: Turner's run out to top of road

parts.note: RO is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run out
taken as written

indicators.note: the top of a word written downwards is its opening letter

parts.note: first letter

explanation.surface: Someone named Turner is run out heading up the road, as if in a cricket report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner' looks like a surname or the painter, but it is simply something that turns.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotor is the rotating part of a machine such as a helicopter or engine, so it is something that spins.

clue.text: Surprised interjection about bottom is relatively rude

indicators.note: about means going around, so the exclamation is placed on either side of the next word

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of astonishment
British slang for the backside

explanation.surface: Exclaiming about someone's backside is rather vulgar.
explanation.walkthrough: Cor is a British expression of surprise, like 'gosh'.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarser is the comparative of coarse, meaning more vulgar or crude in language.

clue.text: Yellow flower border in everyday language

indicators.note: in places the edging word inside the word for plain speech

parts.note: prose is ordinary language as opposed to verse
a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: A gardener describes a bed edged with yellow blooms in plain words.
explanation.definitionFit: The primrose is a pale yellow spring wildflower, and its name is also used for that shade.

clue.text: An attachment to request place with peace and quiet

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names
ease is a state of rest and tranquillity

explanation.surface: Someone asks politely for a spot that is calm and quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: the word is what children are taught to tack on to every request.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying the polite word turns a bare demand into a courteous request, so it is the add-on to one.

clue.text: Anger during stormy scene

parts.note: in means during, as in 'in the night'

indicators.note: a stormy sea is tossed about, so the letters of the next word are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone loses their temper in the middle of a heated row.
explanation.definitionFit: To incense someone is to make them furious, so the verb means to anger.

clue.text: Murder victim meets his end coming after cartel — jog your memory?

parts.note: a ring is a group of people working together illegally
Abel was killed by his brother Cain in Genesis
'his' refers back to the victim, so this is the last letter of his name

explanation.surface: A detective story: the victim's death came after a run-in with a criminal gang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'His end' points back to the victim: the last letter of his own name follows it. To ring a bell is to seem familiar.
explanation.definitionFit: If something rings a bell it stirs a faint recollection, which is what jogging your memory does.

clue.text: Keep quiet about amateur artist's name

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the hushing word wraps around what follows

parts.note: sh is the call for silence
A is a standard abbreviation for amateur
RA is a Royal Academician, the crossword's usual artist

explanation.surface: Someone is told to stay silent about a hobby painter's identity.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarah is a common female first name, so it is one example of a name.

clue.text: Coffee perhaps? How fast it drips into jug when left out for short time

indicators.note: one letter goes out and another comes in its place, in exchange for it

parts.words: How fast it drips into jug
parts.note: the speed at which a vessel fills is its fill rate
L is the abbreviation for left
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A coffee maker's drip rate is described as it fills the jug.
explanation.walkthrough: In FILL RATE one L is swapped for T. The surface coffee is also the definition, the liquid that comes through a filter.
explanation.definitionFit: Filtrate is liquid that has passed through a filter, and filter coffee is one such liquid.

clue.text: Yellow bird, a short-tailed duck crossing channel? Yes

indicators.note: a tail cut short means the final letter of the word is removed

parts.note: across the English Channel, in France, a duck is a canard
Y is the abbreviation for yes, as on a Y/N form

explanation.surface: Is the yellow bird just a stubby duck that flew over the Channel? Apparently so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crossing channel' looks like an insertion, but it sends the duck to France to become CANARD, which loses its D.
explanation.definitionFit: The canary is a small finch kept as a cage bird and famous for its bright yellow plumage.

clue.text: Narcos' bust could be the start of great things

indicators.note: something bust is broken, so the letters are broken up and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A police raid on drug traffickers might launch a big career.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition alludes to the proverb 'great oaks from little acorns grow'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mighty oak trees grow from these small nuts, so they are the humble seeds of something large.

clue.text: Ashen but surprisingly brown

indicators.note: something that happens surprisingly comes out unexpectedly, so the letters appear in an unexpected order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone looked pale yet turned out tanned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brown' looks like an adjective but is the verb, to tan in the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying in the sunshine is how people tan, so to sunbathe is to brown oneself.

clue.text: A neat worker? Good. Roger wilco, out

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the gathered letters are reshuffled

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good
in radio talk roger stands for R, received
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tidy employee signs off a radio call with 'Roger, wilco, out'.
explanation.walkthrough: Neat is an old word for cattle, so a neat worker tends cows, not a tidy one.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat is an archaic word for cattle, and a cowgirl is a woman who herds them.

clue.text: VIP enraged after sacking director on the fiddle according to rumour

indicators.note: being on the fiddle means acting crookedly, so the letters are bent out of order
sacking someone removes them, so the letter for the boss is dropped from what precedes

parts.note: taken as written
D is the abbreviation for director

explanation.surface: Gossip has it that a furious celebrity fired a fraudulent boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Enraged' looks like the anagram signal, but it is fodder; 'on the fiddle' does that job.
explanation.definitionFit: The grapevine is the informal network by which gossip spreads, so it stands for rumour itself.

clue.text: It's not worthy of being eaten in a stew in Belize

indicators.note: the mixed letters are being held inside the abbreviation that follows

parts.note: BH is Belize's international country code, from British Honduras

indicators.note: a stew is a jumbled mixture, so the eaten letters are stirred up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dish is so poor nobody in Belize would eat it in a stew.
explanation.walkthrough: BH, the old British Honduras code, goes around the mixed letters.
explanation.definitionFit: If a task is beneath you it is unworthy of your dignity or status.

clue.text: After destroying string of characters Transylvanian vampire's come to the light of day

definitions.text: come to the light of day

indicators.note: a run of consecutive letters in the middle is wiped out, leaving the two ends

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A vampire from Transylvania emerges into daylight after a killing spree, which is surely fatal.
explanation.walkthrough: The run YLVANIANVAM is deleted from the middle of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To transpire is to become known or come out, as when facts emerge.

clue.text: Crosses from east to west in the creative world

indicators.note: from one direction to the other signals a change, one letter swapped for another

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for east
W is the abbreviation for west
the arts covers painting, music, literature and the like

explanation.surface: Someone travels across the globe within the artistic community.
explanation.walkthrough: In THE ARTS, the E becomes W.
explanation.definitionFit: To thwart someone is to cross them, blocking or frustrating their plans.

clue.text: Throat regularly blocked by dull pain in its passage

indicators.note: a passage blocked by something has it lodged inside
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: first, third and fifth letters
an ache is a dull continuous pain

explanation.surface: A sore throat feels repeatedly obstructed by a dull pain as you swallow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Its' points back to the throat, so the definition is the throat's passage, not the throat itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The trachea is the windpipe, the airway running down through the throat to the lungs.

clue.text: Macho sort, we hear, might get the sack?

indicators.note: we hear points to how the words sound when spoken rather than how they are spelt

parts.note: a very masculine fellow

explanation.surface: A tough guy could be fired from his job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get the sack' means be fired, but here the sack is the postbag.
explanation.definitionFit: A US postman carries a mailbag, so he is someone who is handed a sack to carry.

clue.text: Times of gold and free nuts around start of Michaelmas

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the mixed letters wrap the initial
free means loosened, so the letters are let loose to rearrange

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the feast's name is wanted

parts.note: first letter

explanation.surface: Autumn is pictured as a golden season of falling nuts around the feast of St Michael.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times of gold' reads as the definition, but gold is AU; Michaelmas is 29 September.
explanation.definitionFit: Autumns are the seasons of the year between summer and winter, so they are periods or times.

clue.text: Imperatives of existence and ownership make us act well

parts.note: the command form of the verb of being
the command form of the verb of possessing

explanation.surface: A philosophical claim that commands to exist and to possess make us virtuous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Imperatives' covers both halves: the bare command forms of two verbs.
explanation.definitionFit: To behave is to conduct oneself properly, the thing a parent tells a misbehaving child to do.

clue.text: Become sore as value is attached to bad clue

indicators.note: bad means faulty, so the letters are in the wrong order and must be fixed

parts.note: taken as written
to rate is to value or appraise

explanation.surface: A setter gets annoyed when a poor clue is given a rating.
explanation.definitionFit: To ulcerate is to develop an ulcer, an open sore on the skin or a membrane.

clue.text: Yellow mark seen in Spanish city

indicators.note: seen in means positioned inside, so the currency letter sits within the city name

parts.note: León is a city in north-west Spain
M is the abbreviation for the German mark

explanation.surface: A yellow stain is spotted in a Spanish town.
explanation.walkthrough: M goes inside LEON.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemon is the pale yellow colour of the citrus fruit's skin, used as a colour name.

clue.text: Troublesome fly set to torment again

indicators.note: to torment is to twist and rack, so the letters are wrenched into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
the same word a second time

explanation.surface: An annoying insect is ready to pester someone once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Again' doubles the word, giving six letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The tsetse is an African biting fly that spreads sleeping sickness, so it is a dangerous pest.

clue.text: A noble girl. See the light around her!

indicators.note: the surrounding words wrap around her, so the name lies inside them

parts.note: found across the word boundaries

explanation.surface: A girl of noble birth has a halo shining around her.
explanation.walkthrough: The name is hidden in 'sEE THE Light'. It comes from Old English æthel, meaning noble.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethel is a girl's name derived from the Old English word for noble.

clue.text: One politician's desire (toppling the leader) is mischievous

indicators.note: toppling a leader removes the one at the head, so the first letter goes

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a Member of Parliament
a wish is a desire

explanation.surface: A politician's ambition to overthrow the party leader is naughty.
explanation.walkthrough: WISH loses its first letter to become ISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Impish describes playful, mischievous behaviour, like that of a little imp.

clue.text: Amateur medium taken in by roguish appearance

indicators.note: something taken in by another is swallowed up within it

parts.note: arch means playfully mischievous
M is the abbreviation for medium
an air is a manner or appearance

explanation.surface: A novice spiritualist is fooled by a con artist's looks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Medium' suggests a séance, but it is just the size abbreviation inside ARCH.
explanation.definitionFit: An armchair critic or general theorises without practical experience, so the word means amateur.

clue.text: Too young for nude swimming craze

indicators.note: swimming suggests moving about freely, so the letters float into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
a rage is a fashion or craze

explanation.surface: Someone is too young to join in the latest skinny-dipping fad.
explanation.definitionFit: Underage means below the legal age for something, so too young to be allowed.

clue.text: Seasoned traveller at the front leads astray

indicators.note: going astray means wandering off course, so the letters stray from their order
the front of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: first letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: An experienced traveller at the head of the group takes everyone the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seasoned traveller' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that is seasoned has had salt or spices added for flavour, so salted is a kind of seasoned.
